title: Screening and Characterization of Alkaline Laccase from Novel Bacterium for Decolorization of Congo Red Azo Dye
content: Laccase (EC 1.10.3.2), a multicopper oxidase, is widely recognized for its capacity to oxidize a variety of substrates using molecular oxygen. Initially isolated from the Japanese lacquer tree, its biotechnological potential has prompted renewed interest, particularly in bioremediation applications. This study focuses on a novel alkaline laccase produced by Plesiomonas shigelloides KS116, isolated from an urban waste disposal site in Addis Ababa. Following optimization of growth conditions, laccase activity reached a peak of 83.73 ± 0.63 U/mg after purification through ammonium sulfate precipitation and fast protein liquid chromatography (FPLC), with a molecular weight of 63 kDa. The enzyme displayed optimal activity at pH 8.0 and 40 °C, with Copper sulfate significantly enhancing laccase production. Notably, P. shigelloides KS116 achieved 99% decolorization of the synthetic azo dye Congo red (C32H22N6Na2O6S) within 48 hours, underscoring its practical application in environmental remediation. Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) analysis confirmed the breakdown of azo bonds, validating the biotransformation efficacy. These findings illuminate the potential of P. shigelloides KS116 as a sustainable source of laccase for industrial purposes, particularly in textile wastewater treatment. This research contributes valuable insights into microbial enzyme applications in bioremediation, highlighting an innovative approach to mitigating environmental pollution and advancing sustainability efforts.
